title: WPMS/184/2019 of M/S B. K. INDUSTRIES PATAL DEVI, ALMORA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 184 of 2019
B.K. Industries

Present : Mr. Vikas Anand, Advocate with Mr. B.S. Koranga,
Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Yogesh Pandey, Additional Chief Standing Counsel
with Mr. Suyash Pant, Brief Holder for the
State/respondent nos. 1, 2 & 4.
Mr. K.K. Harbola, Advocate with Mr. Manoj Lakhchaura,
Advocate for respondent no. 3.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.
 The petitioner before this Court claims to be a
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise. He relies upon a
Government Order dated 19.03.2014 by which the State
Government or any instrumentality of the State,
including the local bodies have been instructed to give
30% of the value of the work in a year to a Micro, Small
and Medium Enterprise.
2. Now the newly created Town Area Committee,
which is known as Nagar Panchayat Bhikiyasain,
District Almora for the first time on 26.12.2018 invited
tenders for installation of street light, LED light and

2
solar lights. In other words, it was for public utility
services. In response to the tender, many eligible
applicants applied. The petitioner, however, did not
apply and insisted that the work be given to him under
the provisions of Government Order dated 19.03.2014.
3. The contention of the Nagar Panchayat before
this Court is that they were not aware of the
Government Order dated 19.03.2014 and they asked the
petitioner to take the requisite form, which was for Rs.
1,000/- (Rupees One Thousand only), and apply like
other candidates and if such a benefit is liable to be
given to him that shall be considered. The petitioner,
however, did not apply and instead filed a writ petition
before this Court during vacations, in which a learned
Single Judge of this Court passed the following orders
on 16.01.2019:-
ìMr. Vikas Anand, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. S.R. Joshi, Standing Counsel
along with Mr. Akshay Latwal, Brief
Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.
Heard learned counsel for the
parties.
 Admit.
As prayed, four weeksí time is
granted to the State Counsel to file
counter affidavit.
List this matter immediately after
winter vacations.
Respondents are directed to permit
the petitioner to provisionally participate
in the ongoing tender process at his own
risk. However, the same shall be subject
to final outcome of the present writ
petition.
Urgency application being IA No.
653/2019 stands disposed of.
Let a certified copy of this order be
issued to the learned counsel for the

3
parties immediately today itself on
payment of usual charges.î
4. As of now, the position is that the work for
which the tender was invited has been stalled.
5. The State Counsel does not deny the veracity
of the Government Order dated 19.03.2014, but
according to the State Counsel he is not sure about the
amount of work pursuant to the advertisement in
question, inasmuch as if the value of the work is less
than Rs. 5,00,000/- (Rupees Fie Lakh only) then the
said Government Order will not be applicable.
6. In my considered view, however, the benefit
as sought by the petitioner in the present case cannot
be granted for the reasons that the petitioner has not
given full details before this Court to make out a case
that in case this contract is not given to him or similarly
situated persons, it would be in violation of the
Government Order dated 19.03.2014. There is no
embargo in the Government Order for State or its
instrumentalities, including the local bodies, for not
calling the tender. The instructions are only that 30% of
the total value of work may be given to Micro, Small and
Medium Enterprises. Thirty per cent of the total value of
work may still be available in the coming year and there
is nothing on record to suggest that 30 % of work is not
available. Secondly, Nagar Panchayat Bhikiyasain is a
newly constituted Nagar Panchayat and the work in
question is being done for public utility. Any
interference on the plea of the petitioner would cause
harm to general public as they will be deprived of a
public utility.

4
7. In view therefore, the writ petitions fail and
are hereby dismissed. It is, however, made clear that
this Court has not said anything regarding the
applicability of the Government Order dated
19.03.2014.
(Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
 25.06.2019
